summary: Radar for 2026-11-05 22:00 UTC, GLP-1 focus. The best openings are calendar-driven or already in our Lane A queue. Thanksgiving momentum keeps climbing (86, seen 10×, peak 18–27 Nov). Injection-site reactions, fatigue and dehydration are this week's Lane A long-forms. Cold-and-flu season adds a fresh hook for a "sick on tirzepatide" or dehydration piece. Fresh news I checked: (1) Lilly's 5 Nov press release confirms new data at ACR Convergence. TRIUMPH-4 (retatrutide, knee OA) is a plenary on 8 Nov and TRIUMPH-1 a poster on 10 Nov. It also includes TOGETHER-PsA, a randomized phase 3b of tirzepatide + ixekizumab vs ixekizumab alone in psoriatic arthritis with obesity. Both are good 13:00 Short leads. (2) ObesityWeek (14–17 Nov) may give the full REDEFINE 4 results: CagriSema vs tirzepatide, open-label, in obesity. This is the only likely trigger for an L2 head-to-head long-form, and only within 48 h of release. (3) Rogaine's 30% sales surge, linked to GLP-1 use (BoF, 5 Nov), plus the Straight Arrow risk explainer, confirm that hair is our highest-demand body worry. Use it to refresh the fixed hair long-form and its links. No hair Shorts this week, per the playbook. (4) The ABC 'Zepbound beats Wegovy' story (4 Nov) resurfaces SURMOUNT-5 (751 adults without diabetes, about 20% vs 14%), so it isn't new data. It can carry one head-to-head Short with tirzepatide named first. (5) The 'natural Ozempic' BRP story (ScienceDaily, 4 Nov) is a 2025 Nature study in mice and minipigs with no human trials, so it's caution / myth-check only. (6) The prediabetes GLP-1 vs metformin study (AHA, observational, not peer-reviewed) is peaking in Reuters, Fox and US News. Rejected: retatrutide online-sales coverage, telehealth and self-pay dispensing launches, generic semaglutide approvals in Brazil (cost/access), the Daily Wire teens piece and the Wernicke case-report clickbait. Some details are still unverified: the PubMed abstracts wouldn't load (cookie wall), and the TOGETHER-PsA endpoint wording only came from secondary sites. Downstream agents must confirm those against the primary records.

candidates.topic: Thanksgiving on tirzepatide: feeling full fast, protein first, smaller plates, alcohol and easing nausea at a big meal
candidates.angle: A calm 'Will Thanksgiving dinner make me sick on tirzepatide?' Short series, each ending with the funnel line to the live Thanksgiving long-form. One new practical fact per Short: slower gastric emptying means fullness comes early, start with protein, sip don't gulp, and alcohol may hit differently. Add the prescriber line.
candidates.why_now: Seen in 10 snapshots with momentum climbing steadily from 78 to 86. Event-menu and food-industry coverage (Cater + Event, 5 Nov) shows the 'GLP-1 plate' is going mainstream. Our Thanksgiving long-form is live but slow (143 impressions, 17 min), so Shorts and links from the big three should feed it before the peak.

evidence.signal: 'The Plate Has Changed: How GLP-1 Medications Are Reshaping Event Menus' shows holiday and event eating on GLP-1 going mainstream

candidates.angle: Lane A long-form 'Tirzepatide Injection Site Reactions: What's Normal'. Open on a 'you just noticed a red patch' scenario. Use the label's reported rates, separate common and temporary reactions from signs worth a call, and cover our own non-sourced habits (no tags). Include the prescriber line. Thumbnail state change: worried → answered.

candidates.why_now: Seen 10 times, momentum rising from 72 to 84. Its Short hit 226 views by day 3 (our 3rd-best body-worry Short). It's in this week's Lane A ship list and sits right next to Side Effects, which helps related-video pickup.

candidates.topic: Why am I so tired on tirzepatide? Label fatigue rates of 5% (5 mg), 6% (10 mg) and 7% (15 mg) vs 3% on placebo
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form. The first line answers it: fatigue is a listed but uncommon side effect, at 5–7% vs 3% on placebo. Then the likely everyday contributors (eating less, fluids, protein, sleep), each worded carefully, plus when tiredness is a reason to call the prescriber. Use the NHS tiredness page (2023 revision) for general causes.
keywords: why am i so tired on zepbound
candidates.predicted_peak: Steady evergreen; seasonal bump as winter starts
candidates.why_now: Seen 5+ times and stable at 80–82. It's in this week's Lane A ship list, and the fatigue Short already exists as a funnel source. Shorter days in November add a natural 'winter tiredness' hook.

evidence.signal: Label fatigue rates of 5–7% vs 3% on placebo, named in the playbook as a Lane A target

candidates.topic: Sick on tirzepatide this cold and flu season: dehydration signs, vomiting or diarrhoea, and when to call your prescriber (the label's acute kidney injury warning)
candidates.angle: Lane A long-form 'Tirzepatide and Dehydration: Signs and What Helps', framed for the season: you catch a stomach bug or flu while you're already eating less. Cover the label's warning on dehydration from vomiting or diarrhoea, plain warning signs, and fluids (our own tips, no tags). Advise calling the prescriber about sick-day plans, and give no stop or skip advice. Include the don't-stop line.
candidates.why_now: Seasonal cycle starting. Seen in earlier snapshots at 74–80. It's in this week's Lane A list, and a new 5 Nov cohort study on NSAIDs and GI bleeding with GLP-1 adds a 'which cold medicines?' question that people search for.

candidates.topic: Retatrutide and knee osteoarthritis pain: what's confirmed from TRIUMPH-4 (ACR plenary, 8 Nov) and TRIUMPH-1 (poster, 10 Nov)
candidates.angle: 13:00 'What's confirmed?' Short with a loop ending: average change in WOMAC knee pain score, up to 4.5 points (75.8%) vs placebo over 68 weeks in adults with obesity and knee OA, and more than 1 in 8 pain-free. Every number gets its measure, arm and comparator. Add the 'not approved; online research products aren't the trial drug' line.

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide plus ixekizumab for psoriatic arthritis with obesity: TOGETHER-PsA, a randomized phase 3b at ACR 2026
candidates.angle: 13:00 fresh randomized result: 'Does tirzepatide help arthritis drugs work better?' Explain the design (combination vs ixekizumab alone, adults with active PsA and obesity), the composite endpoint in plain words, and that it's one trial. Weight loss is framed as one measure among joint outcomes. Not yet an approved use; talk to your rheumatologist or prescriber.
candidates.why_now: Randomized, tirzepatide-named, and presented at ACR this week. It fits the 'benefits beyond weight / inflammation' pillar with very thin creator coverage. Lilly's 5 Nov press release confirms it's on the programme.
